# Iceland Summer 2024

## Overview

I flew into Keflavik on 4 July 2024 and picked up a campervan from a depot near the airport. Ten days with a diesel heater, a two-burner stove and a bed that folded out over the cab. I planned the loop loosely and booked nothing except the first night at a campsite outside Reykjavik. The weather sat near 11 degrees most days, rain sideways on two afternoons and one clear evening at midnight that never got properly dark.

## Route

I drove the Ring Road clockwise, which meant the south coast first. Reykjavik to Vik took a full day with stops at Seljalandsfoss and the black beach at Reynisfjara. From Vik I pushed east to Hofn, past the glacier lagoon at Jokulsarlon, where I camped two nights and watched icebergs drift out to sea. Then the long northern stretch, the east fjords and a slow climb to Akureyri, which I used as a base for three days of day trips. The last leg swung west to Snaefellsnes, where I walked the coast path at Arnarstapi and camped one night under the mountain. The odometer read 2100 km at drop-off, which matched my rough estimate almost exactly and left the van with an empty tank and a boot full of wet towels.

## Costs

Fuel was the big surprise. Diesel ran about 3.20 euros a litre and the van averaged 11 litres per hundred kilometres, so the driving alone came to roughly 540 euros. Campsites were 15 to 25 euros a night with electricity, less if I skipped the hookup. Food from the Bonus supermarket kept me near 20 euros a day. Eating out once in Akureyri cost 45 euros for lamb soup and a beer. The campervan rental was 1800 euros for the ten days including insurance. Total spend landed near 3100 euros.
